title: Collateral Policy on Late-Received Certificates — Grain and Livestock Values, Operating Lines of Credit
content:
How many calendar days after its as-of date an Operating Lines of Credit borrowing base certificate was received decides how much of its stated unpriced stored grain and market livestock values counts.

## Rule

The stated unpriced stored grain value and the stated market livestock value are each taken at:

- **0.8 times the stated amount** when the certificate was received more than 30 calendar days after its as-of date;
- **0.9 times the stated amount** when it was received more than 15 but no more than 30 calendar days after it;
- **the stated amount** when it was received no more than 15 calendar days after it.

The as-of date itself is day 0. The advance rate for each of the two classes then acts on the value so taken.

## Receipt lag table (hypothetical certificate with an as-of date of 1 May)

| Date received | Days after the as-of date | Grain and livestock taken at |
|---|---|---|
| 16 May | 15 | The stated amount |
| 17 May | 16 | 0.9 times the stated amount |
| 31 May | 30 | 0.9 times the stated amount |
| 1 June | 31 | 0.8 times the stated amount |

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

A certificate received 20 days after its as-of date states USD 500,000 of unpriced stored grain. The value taken is 0.9 times USD 500,000, that is USD 450,000; at a 75% advance rate on stored grain that class then lends USD 337,500.
